newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia Nov deficit 523.1 mln rgt.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia Nov deficit 523.1 mln rgt.

text.p: Following are reactions to the announcement by Malaysia's Statistics Department that the trade deficit in November was 523.1 million ringgit and 1.5 billion ringgit for the first 11 months of 1996.

A Reuters survey of economists from 10 research houses earlier this week forecast an average trade deficit of 148 million ringgit for November, though their estimates varied widely, from a surplus of 700 million ringgit to a deficit of 700 million ringgit.
LEW YIN SZE, CHIEF ECONOMIST OF J.M. SASSOON IN SINGAPORE:
"The improvement in the deficit coming this year has been quite strong. There was a slight deterioration in the trade deficit in 1996.
"We were forecasting a sharp improvement. I had the trade balance at zero for the full year 1996 with a current account deficit of 11-12 billion ringgit.
"Given the november numbers, the currenct account now looks like 13 billion ringgit for the full year. Still it's a sharp improvement over the 18 billion in 1995."
NG BOK ENG, REGIONAL ECONOMIST AT DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL IN SINGAPORE:
"I think it was slightly disappointing. But I don't think it will have any impact on the market.
"The full-year number will be much better. We have one more month left. I think it (the full-year deficit) will be lower than the official forecast (9.64 billion ringgit).
"The question is what the trade numbers mean for this year.
"While we have benign import numbers, it's the export side which will help. (The deficit) will start to improve once exports improve."
SONG SENG WUN, REGIONAL ECONOMIST AT H.G. ASIA IN SINGAPORE
"We were expecting a deficit of 331 million, but it's going in the same direction. The November deficit was due to capital imports for the oil and gas industry in Sarawak. We are not unduly alarmed.

"The December figures should show the deificit for the whole of 1996 to be around 1.2 to 1.3 billion ringgit. This will be better than the full year projection by the Ministry of Finance in the October budget.
"The weaker yen and the stronger ringgit should help the import side, and the improving deficit should give continuing support for the ringgit."
